pageCache.text:
Sports Premium
The Government provides funding to ensure the development of high quality sport within schools. This is around £16k plus an amount per pupil depending on the number of pupil on roll. Schools use the funding to create a long term sustainable sports plan which includes high-quality staff training, support for schools from local Schools Games Officers (our link is based at Mountbatten School) and potentially equipment. All classes at NBJS receive at least one hour of indoor PE (gymnastics/dance) and one hour of outdoor games. A wide variety of clubs is offered - some chargeable from outside providers - others run by school staff.
As a school we have adopted a whole school approach to the Active Mile, which takes place in the last 15 minutes of the lunch-time break.

Supporting your Child's Education & SEN
Inclusion and Special Educational Needs and Disabilities at NBJS
North Baddesley Junior School is committed to the meaningful inclusion of all pupils within our school community. Through working to identify needs early in conjunction with families, we seek to remove barriers to learning so that pupils can thrive in learning through a broad and balanced curriculum.
As a staff team, we have worked on a definition of inclusion which we seek to adopt in the classroom:
Enquiries about an individual child’s progress should be addressed at first to the class teacher since they are the person who knows the child best. Other enquiries can be addressed to Mrs Daas – SENDCo. Please make an appointment with the school office if you wish to speak to the SENDCo.
Universal Support as ordinarily available for your child
All children receive responsive support in their learning journeys through regular teacher assessment of their learning. Our focus is that all children, including those with SEND, receive high quality teaching and that learning is adapted according to their emerging needs.
Targeted Support and the SEND Register
Some pupils who have a SEND need, which has been identified in line with the school’s SEND Policy and Identification flow chart, benefit from further SEN Support where our SENDCo will have discussed placing your child on the school’s SEND Register. This would be supported through detailed analysis and reflection of your child’s needs (including attainment, progress and behaviour).
As a result of this, your child’s progress will be closely monitored through setting termly targets in an Individual Learning Plan (ILP) written by the class teacher which you will receive with your child’s report.
The Assess, Plan, Do, Review process allows teachers to set personalised targets for your child, plan their learning and reflect and adapt accordingly.
When your child is making progress and consistently achieving their targets, they may be removed from the SEN register, in discussion with families, and remain closely monitored by the school to ensure good progress is maintained.
Where your child has a higher level of need, and with parental permission, the school may need to seek advice from external agencies. These agencies include:
Education, Health and Care Plans
Where some children, who have complex and long-term needs, may need more support than SEN support or the school’s own resources can provide, requests for individual assessment for Education, Health and Care Plans can be made to the local authority. The aim of these plans is to collate support from health and social care alongside the school with their individual SEND in mind. Decision making around this process would be discussed with the school SENDCo.
The 2015 SEND Code of Practice explains that:
“Where, despite the school having taken relevant and purposeful action to identify, assess and meet the SEN of the child or young person, the child or young person has not made expected progress, the school or parents should consider requesting an Education Health and Care needs assessment.” (6.63 CoP, 2015)
Enquiries about Inclusion and SEND at the school should be addressed to Miss Verlander – SENDCo. Please make an appointment with the school office if you wish to speak to the SENDCo.
We are continuously trying to make sure that our school is fully accessible for pupils and adults. Our recent cladding project has allowed us to incorporate a second accessible toilet - so we now have one at either end of the ground floor. We have also moved the ICT suite and Music rooms downstairs. The design of the building on two floors means that 4 classrooms are only accessible via stairs. Nevertheless, there is step free access to the whole of the ground floor. In the Reception area, we have inductive loop hearing assistance and a lowered counter height. The number of disabled parking bays has doubled. The main Reception door is also power assisted.

What is my child learning at school?
At North Baddesley Junior School, we have adapted and refined the National Curriculum to create broad and balanced, exciting and relevant experiences that encourage the children to be actively involve in their learning. Children are offered a range of opportunities to work as part of a team, as well as develop their independence and resilience. The opportunities we provide at North Baddesley Junior School aim to inspire children, develop a love of learning and support them as they become young adults.

Useful school information (Holidays & INSET, dinners, uniform,sickness)
We return to school on Tuesday September 1st 2026.
INSET Days 2026/2027
North Baddesley Infant School and North Baddesley Junior School have collaborated to ensure that INSET days across both schools are identical for the academic year 2026-2027.
You will note that four of the days, (November 2026 and June 2027) enable families to take a long weekend outside of peak holiday times. The February day should allow greater flexibility for returning home from travelling at the end of the February half term holiday for breaks. In recent years, we recognise that a greater proportion of families are looking for more cost-effective family time. This has impacted on pupil attendance and access to education. We hope that by sharing this information early supports the attendance of every child for the academic year 2026-2027. We have to balance INSET days with professional development requirements for the teams at both NBIS and NBJS across the year. Nevertheless, having all children in school for the maximum time remains our priority.
Schools allocate 5 extra days for INSET training. If convenient, we try to link with the Infant School for dates to alleviate childcare, but this isn't always possible because of different needs and requirements for training within each school.
The standard Hampshire School calendar can be accessed via the link below:
https://www.hants.gov.uk/educationandlearning/schoolholidays
In 2026/2027 the Junior & Infant INSET days coincide and fall on the following dates. Due to the exceptional circumstances, these may be subject to unexpected late change, but we have commitments for training on the days so we hope there will be no changes during the year:
Please note that school holidays do not necessarily match those of our link secondary school, Mountbatten. Please check their website for information.
Link to NBJS page on Hampshire County Council's website
http://www3.hants.gov.uk/schooldetails?dfes=2265#schooldetails
Payments using Tucasi
This system allows you to make payments for school dinners, trips and music lessons.
This is an external payment system and can be accessed via this link:
https://www.scopay.com/northbaddesley-jun?redirect=true
Our main colour theme is bottle green and all items of uniform (except sweatshirt/cardigan with a logo) are available from major retail outlets as part of their generic offering.
Grey or black school trousers or tailored school shorts
Grey or black school skirts - green checked summer dress
Sweatshirts or cardigans with or without the school logo.
White polo (with or without logo) or white collared shirts/blouses
Sensible all-black school shoes
Each child is allocated to a house and should have a sports t-shirt in the appropriate colour (red/sky blue/green/yellow. Plain t-shirts are acceptable but not with other branding.
Black or navy blue shorts for indoor gym and outdoors or jogging bottoms for outdoor sport when the weather is cold.
Appropriate footwear for the type of activity (trainers/boots for outdoors, indoor PE is done bare-foot)
(Shinpads & football boots are a requirement when playing in area tournaments - we do have limited loan equipment)

Visions and Values
Our ethos, visions and values
Our visions and values are at the core of everything we do. They underpin our teaching and learning, and provide an environment which prepares our pupils as confident, happy citizens.
“Respectful hearts, Aspiring minds, Resilient spirits."
“Be kind, dream big, keep going!"
At North Baddesley Junior School, we are a community built on Respect, driven by the courage to Aspire, and strengthened by our shared Resilience. We empower every child to grow into a thoughtful, confident learner who strives for their best, supports others, and meets challenges with determination.
Our Vision
At North Baddesley Junior School, we are a community built on Respect, driven by the courage to Aspire, and strengthened by our shared Resilience. These values shape every aspect of school life and guide us in creating a nurturing, ambitious environment where all children feel seen, supported, and inspired.
We believe that every child has unique strengths, talents, and dreams. Our vision is to empower each learner to grow into a thoughtful, confident individual who values themselves and others. Through a rich, stimulating curriculum and a culture of high expectations, we encourage pupils to strive for their personal best—academically, socially, and emotionally.
At North Baddesley, Respect is the foundation of our relationships and community. Children learn to celebrate differences, show kindness, and recognise the contribution of each individual. We foster a sense of belonging where every voice is valued and every child feels safe to express themselves.
We inspire pupils to Aspire boldly. By providing engaging learning experiences, meaningful challenges, and opportunities to explore new interests, we help children develop curiosity, independence, and a genuine love of learning. We support them to set goals, reflect on their achievements, and recognise their own potential.
Through developing Resilience, we prepare our children for the challenges of the future. We teach them to persevere, embrace mistakes as part of learning, and approach new situations with confidence and courage. Our pupils learn that growth is a journey and that determination helps them succeed both in school and in life.
Working in partnership with families and the wider community, we are committed to preparing our children to be compassionate, capable, and responsible individuals—ready to thrive, contribute positively to society, and carry our values forward into the world.
